The procedure and typical related perioperative care
Only the surgery, with each follow-up visit billed
Complications requiring a return to the OR

explanation: Global surgical package covers the operation and routine related care in the global period.

distractorExplanations.a: Unrelated E/M visits are billed separately (modifier 24), and globals last 0, 10, or 90 days.
distractorExplanations.c: Routine related follow-up visits are included in the package, not billed separately.
distractorExplanations.d: Complications that need a return to the OR are billed separately with modifier 78.

prompt: The same root operation is repeated at different body sites that have distinct values in the body-part character. Per ICD-10-PCS guidelines, you should:

options.text: Report a separate code for each distinct body-part value
Report one code for the most significant site only
Report the code once and note the extra sites in the 7th character
Append a modifier to the code to show the multiple sites

explanation: Guideline B3.2a: code multiple procedures separately when the same root operation is performed on different body parts defined by distinct values of the body-part character.

distractorExplanations.b: Coding one site under-reports distinct procedures.
distractorExplanations.c: The 7th character is the qualifier; it does not capture additional sites, so each distinct body-part value needs its own code.
distractorExplanations.d: ICD-10-PCS has no modifiers; site modifiers such as XS belong to CPT/HCPCS outpatient coding.

prompt: A laparoscopic procedure is converted to open and completed through the open incision. Per ICD-10-PCS guidelines, code:

options.text: Only the laparoscopic (percutaneous endoscopic) procedure
The open procedure plus a percutaneous endoscopic Inspection
The open procedure, with the conversion noted by a qualifier
Both the full laparoscopic and full open procedures

explanation: Guideline B3.2d: when the intended root operation is attempted by one approach and converted to another, code the completed procedure with its approach plus an Inspection for the abandoned approach.

distractorExplanations.a: The procedure was completed open, so coding only the laparoscopic approach is wrong.
distractorExplanations.c: No qualifier captures a conversion; guideline B3.2d requires a separate percutaneous endoscopic Inspection code.
distractorExplanations.d: The procedure was performed once; the laparoscopic part is an Inspection only.

prompt: Amputation of a finger through the proximal phalanx is coded to which ICD-10-PCS root operation?

options.text: Resection
Excision
Detachment
Destruction

explanation: Detachment is cutting off all or a portion of an upper or lower extremity, including fingers and toes. The qualifier specifies the level of amputation.

distractorExplanations.a: Resection is not used for extremity amputations.
distractorExplanations.b: Excision removes a portion of a body part but is not used for amputations.
distractorExplanations.d: Destruction eradicates tissue by energy, force, or agent; it does not cut off an extremity.

prompt: In ICD-10-PCS, which approach value describes a procedure performed through a laparoscope inserted via a small skin puncture?

Via Natural or Artificial Opening Endoscopic
Via Natural or Artificial Opening
Percutaneous Endoscopic

prompt: Upcoding is

Reporting a lower level than documented to avoid an audit
Billing separate codes for components of a bundled service
Billing for a service that the provider did not perform

Presenting clinical indicators with options including "other" or "undetermined"

prompt: Under the Medicare HAC–POA program, a CMS-selected hospital-acquired condition that was NOT present on admission will:

Be reported only as a Z code for tracking
Be deleted from the claim before submission
Not count as a CC/MCC to raise MS-DRG payment

distractorExplanations.b: The condition keeps its own diagnosis code; it is not replaced by a Z code.
